articles.title: 86 to 101: Virat Kohli's final ODI window to break Sachin Tendulkar's century record
articles.summary: It was the semi-final of the 2023 World Cup when Virat Kohli scored his 50th ODI century in front of Sachin Tendulkar, surpassing his idol's record of 49
articles.body: It was the semi-final of the 2023 World Cup when Virat Kohli scored his 50th ODI century in front of Sachin Tendulkar, surpassing his idol's record of 49 hundreds in the format. That innings put another Tendulkar record within Kohli's reach. Tendulkar's 100 international centuries remain the benchmark, leaving Kohli with a chance to become the first batter to reach 101.But the equation changed when Kohli retired from Test cricket on May 12, 2025. With his T20I career already over, ODI cricket became his only remaining route to Tendulkar's record. Now, with the 2027 World Cup less than a year away, Kohli has 86 international centuries - 14 short of equalling Tendulkar and 15 away from surpassing him.His latest hundred, a 139 not out against West Indies in the first ODI of the recently concluded series, was followed by 29 in the second match and a golden duck in the third.So how many opportunities does Kohli have left, and can he turn them into the 15 centuries he needs to move past Tendulkar's 100?86 to 101: The century equation beginsIndia currently have 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs scheduled before the 2027 World Cup - five against New Zealand, three against Sri Lanka and three against Zimbabwe. India's World Cup campaign will begin against Australia in Cape Town on October 7, 2027.The new FTP could add another six-match ODI series in South Africa in the weeks before the World Cup, giving India a chance to acclimatise to conditions ahead of the tournament. However, that series is not part of the confirmed schedule as of yet.The Asia Cup is another part of the picture. The 2027 tournament is scheduled to be played in Bangladesh from June 18 to July 4 and is expected to return to the ODI format. A detailed fixture list has not been announced, but based on the 2023 format, India could play up to six matches if they reach the final.The World Cup itself will have five group-stage matches and if the team reaches the Super 7, they will play six more matches, with a semi-final and final to follow if they go all the way. A finalist could therefore play a maximum of 13 matches at the tournament.That leaves Kohli with 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs before the World Cup, with the Asia Cup providing additional opportunities before the tournament.For Kohli, the target remains 15 centuries.India or overseas? The recent pattern in Kohli's centuriesKohli's recent ODI numbers are markedly different at home and overseas. In his last 32 ODI matches in India, he has scored nine centuries. In his last 32 overseas ODIs, he has scored three - in Dubai, Chattogram and Colombo.That split comes into focus with India scheduled to play five ODIs in New Zealand before the World Cup.Kohli's overall record overseas, though, is substantial. He has scored 27 of his 55 ODI centuries outside India. Bangladesh is his most productive overseas country, with six centuries, followed by Sri Lanka and Australia with five each. He has four in the West Indies, three in South Africa and one each in New Zealand, England, Zimbabwe and the UAE.Sri Lanka remains one of Kohli's most productive opponents. Kohli has scored 10 ODI centuries against Sri Lanka, his highest tally against any opponent. The three-match series in December will be played in India, with the ODIs scheduled for December 13, 16 and 19. Zimbabwe follow with three matches on January 3, 6 and 9.2027 World Cup: Kohli's final shot at Sachin's recordKohli's World Cup record gives him a strong base to build on. In 37 World Cup matches, he has scored 1,795 runs at an average of 59.83, with five centuries and 12 half-centuries.The 2023 edition was his most productive World Cup. He scored 765 runs, including three centuries and six half-centuries, and finished as the tournament's leading run-scorer. It was also the tournament in which he scored his 50th ODI century, moving past Tendulkar's record of 49.Only ODI cricket remainsKohli has already crossed 15000 ODI runs, becoming only the second batter after Tendulkar to reach the mark. He did so in his 303rd innings. With Test and T20I cricket behind him, every international century Kohli scores from here will come in ODIs. He has also said that the 2027 World Cup will be his last World Cup for India.Fifteen hundreds remain between Kohli and 101.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We all have huge sympathy': Why England cricket ready to fund West Indies Test
articles.summary: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) could step in financially if needed to ensure England’s women play a Test in the West Indies next spring.
articles.body: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) could step in financially if needed to ensure England’s women play a Test in the West Indies next spring. The match is planned as part of a multi-format series and is considered important preparation for England’s 2027 Ashes campaign.Cricket West Indies (CWI) recently announced several cost-cutting measures, including reductions in player contracts. Earlier this year, it also cancelled a planned women’s Test against Australia, although the rest of that tour went ahead.There have been no talks about cancelling England’s Test, and the wider tour, which includes three T20s and three ODIs, is not currently under threat.Speaking to the BBC, ECB chair Richard Thompson said: "I hope not. That's not expected to be cancelled. I hope it will take place."He also said the ECB would "look at" providing financial help if CWI faced difficulties staging the match.Normally, the host cricket board pays the costs of hosting visiting teams. However, touring in the Caribbean can be expensive because players often need to travel between different islands. CWI said it has spent more than $80m on domestic air travel over the past 15 years.'It's very important for us'Thompson said the ECB wants the Test to happen because England need more red-ball cricket before the Ashes."We want that Test match to play out," said Thompson. "It's very important for us because our first women's match in the Ashes is the Headingley Test, so we need a good red-ball warm-up."We've got to be playing somewhere and we'd much prefer that to be the West Indies."England have played just one Test since their Ashes defeat in early 2025, losing to India at Lord’s. They have not faced West Indies in a women’s Test since 1979, while West Indies last played a Test in 2004.England will also hold a 10-day red-ball training camp in India in January as part of their Ashes preparations.Thompson added: "We all have a huge sympathy for the West Indies, we all want to see a successful West Indian nation. They have very unique challenges and I hope through the International Cricket Council and others we can find a way through this."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'No one treats a human being like that': Ravi Shastri calls out Pakistan's treatment of jailed Imran Khan
articles.summary: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri has spoken out over the reported treatment of jailed former Pakistan captain Imran Khan, calling it “inhumane” and
articles.body: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri has spoken out over the reported treatment of jailed former Pakistan captain Imran Khan, calling it “inhumane” and saying no person should be treated that way.Reports cited in the story claim Khan’s health has worsened in jail, with only 15% vision remaining in his right eye.Shastri backs Imran on humanitarian groundsSpeaking to Republic World, Shastri said he was shocked by Khan’s situation and believed cricketers around the world would share his concerns."I'm not a politician. But just to see the way he's being treated today is shocking. You know, no one treats a human being like that. On humanitarian grounds, I don't think he deserves what he's getting. So I don't speak just for myself. I think there'll be a lot of cricketers around the globe who will be echoing the same sentiments," said Shastri.He also wished Khan good health and praised his achievements as a cricketer and captain, particularly his ability to guide young players."I just hope he's well and his health is good. Because what he gave to the game was something special. And my memories of him are just being an outstanding leader. You know, just a leader of men. The ability to motivate youngsters and then take them through. You said he came close at the age of 40, captain of the side, and he won the World Cup with a pretty young team," he added.'He doesn't deserve it'Shastri said Khan, who has been in jail since 2023, is one of Pakistan’s most recognisable figures worldwide and should receive better treatment."Hopefully. Hope he comes out and is treated better. He's been there for a long time. You could be out somewhere else, in the same position, because I don't understand the politics. But to sit in a cell there, he doesn't deserve it because he's the most recognised Pakistani face globally. Whether you like it or not, that's my view," said Shastri.He also remembered Khan as a great all-rounder and leader, saying the India-Pakistan rivalry was built on mutual respect."This man you're seeing there with me was an unbelievable cricketer. I mean, a great cricketer is an understatement. The rivalry was out of respect."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or Sanju Samson? India face selection dilemma ahead of first T20I against West Indies
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Coming off the golden glow of their Asian Games triumph in Japan, India step into Tuesday’s fivematch T20I series opener against the West Indies
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Coming off the golden glow of their Asian Games triumph in Japan, India step into Tuesday’s fivematch T20I series opener against the West Indies at the Ekana Stadium here carrying momentum, silverware and an intriguing selection headache at the top of the order.While Abhishek Sharma’s explosive presence as a designated opener is virtually etched in ink, the suspense lies in who walks out alongside him. It is a clash of narratives: the breathtaking audacity of youth versus the hardened composure of experience.In one corner stands teen prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, whose fearless strokeplay has set pulses racing across the circuit. In the other is Sanju Samson, the seasoned campaigner whose heroics in India’s 2026 T20 World Cup triumph remains etched in cricketing folklore.Will head coach Gautam Gambhir lean into the romance of the next generation, or will he trust the calm authority of a proven match-winner?Bowling coach Morne Morkel acknowledged the delicate juggling act ahead of the first T20I. “I’m pretty sure Gautam will look to rotate him (Sooryavanshi). That is up to the selectors, and the coach and the captain, in terms of the playing level, or which playing level will be the best to win a game for India on our home soil. In terms of the starting X, he guys just came back from an Asian Games, so we’re going to see how everybody’s feeling after jet lag, after travelling, and then from there, make plans accordingly.”Fatigue, indeed, remains a tangible hurdle. “The red flag, or the problem, might be our guys travelling back and then immediately playing an international match after the Asian Games,” Morkel said. “Some of the guys arrived only a couple of days ago. But I think once we are up and running, and the series gets going, we will be up for it.”The spotlight will also be on skipper Shreyas Iyer. In his last 10 outings at the helm, a half-century has eluded him. Iyer’s blade yielded just 34 runs across two Asian Games fixtures and 48 in three matches against Afghanistan.Fortunately for India, their bowling arsenal welcomes back two electrifying local favourites returning to action after the Zimbabwe tour in July: Mayank Yadav and Prince Yadav.Standing in India’s way is a dangerous West Indies outfit marshalled by Shai Hope, who is in blistering touch following back-to-back ODI centuries.For the Caribbean side, Lucknow is a familiar venue. They spent nearly a month in the city in 2019 when Afghanistan used the Ekana Stadium as their home ground. Though history has rarely been kind to them, yielding just one win and three losses in four T20Is at the venue compared to India’s dominant 3-1 ledger.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India 'A' pacers look to step up to the plate against Australia 'A'
articles.summary: PUDUCHERRY: In an era where 350-plus totals in ODIs are becoming the norm, fast bowlers are often left walking a tightrope.
articles.body: PUDUCHERRY: In an era where 350-plus totals in ODIs are becoming the norm, fast bowlers are often left walking a tightrope. India’s recent ODI series against the West Indies was a case in point, with the bowlers conceding 295 and 405 in the first two games before West Indies chased down 352 in the final ODI with 10 balls to spare.As India look towards the 2027 World Cup, where they begin their campaign against Australia on Oct 7, the threematch one-day series between India ‘A’ and Australia ‘A’ in Puducherry offers another window into the country’s pace reserves.The big question is: who can eventually emerge as the ideal partner for Jasprit Bumrah?With Arshad Khan, Gurjapneet Singh and Yash Thakur are part of the India ‘A’ setup, it will be interesting to see if anyone can step up.India ‘A’ coach Lakshmipathy Balaji believes the cupboard is far from bare. For him, the answer lies as much in patience and nurturing as it does in raw numbers.“Many have potential. High-scoring games are common now, but bowlers will adapt over time. Bumrah became world-class through time, effort and experience. Youngsters like Anshul (Kamboj) and Gurnoor (Brar) need time and grooming to match international demands. It won’t always be 350-400 run games; bowlers will adapt to modern demands very soon,” Balaji said.Anshul Kamboj was handed his ODI debut in the third game against West Indies after Prasidh Krishna was ruled out. It was, however, a baptism of fire as he conceded 82 runs in nine overs. Gurnoor Brar, who has nine ODIs under his belt, also had an expensive series, while Auqib Nabi went for 84 in 8.5 overs on his ODI debut. Prasidh, too, had a difficult outing in his two games.Yet Balaji does not see the recent run-fests as a cause for concern.“Nothing is lacking, everyone is working hard. Since both teams have scored heavily, batting has temporarily moved ahead of bowling in modern cricket. Once bowling units click together, a balanced contest between bat and ball will return soon,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Suryakumar Yadav left out of Mumbai Ranji Trophy squad despite availability: 'He needs more red-ball cricket'
articles.summary: MUMBAI: In another huge boost to his fledgling career and a vote of confidence in his abilities, Mumbai's senior selection committee, led by Rajesh Pawar,
articles.body: MUMBAI: In another huge boost to his fledgling career and a vote of confidence in his abilities, Mumbai's senior selection committee, led by Rajesh Pawar, on Monday appointed opener Ayush Mhatre as the new vice-captain of Mumbai’s Ranji Trophy squad for the first match of the 2026-27 season against Chandigarh from Oct 11 at the Wankhede Stadium, even as they snubbed India's 2026 T20 World Cup winning captain Suryakumar Yadav, who had earlier confirmed his availability and willingness to be a part of Mumbai's Ranji side, on the grounds that he needed to "play more red-ball cricket."The 16-member squad, which will be captained by veteran batter Siddhesh Lad, includes India's Test opener Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sarfaraz Khan.The 36-year-old Suryakumar didn't feature in any of pre-season tournaments for Mumbai, the local Kanga League, and didn't take part in the in Mumbai's intra-squad matches at the Brabourne Stadium and the MCA's ground in BKC recently."If Surya were to be picked, Musheer Khan, who scored 96 for West Zone in the Duleep Trophy in Aug, would have had to be dropped. That wasn't feasible," a source in the Mumbai Cricket Association told TOI.The selection committee was attended by former India skipper Dilip Vengsarkar, who is the MCA's Cricket Advisor."Surya is available but it was thought to go with the youngsters for the time being. He is obviously a big-match player and a proven performer for Mumbai. We just want to get into rhythm by playing a few red-ball matches. Surya hasn’t played a red-ball match for the last 18 months, so we want him to have a few games under his belt and then he can get into the team," Pawar told reporters.Throwing light on the appointment of Lad and Mhatre as the new captain and vice-captain of the Mumbai team, Pawar said, "The selection committee unanimously has gone with experienced Siddhesh Lad as the captain for the seasons. Along with a senior, we have planned to groom a junior in Ayush as the vice-captain. He has led the India Under-19 to the (U-19) World Cup win, is a smart cricketer and is in excellent nick."TOI had reported about veteran seam bowling allrounder Shardul Thakur suffering from a hand injury during a practice match at the Cricket Club of India after being struck by a ball hit by Mhatre and is likely to miss a few matches initially of Mumbai's 2026-27 Ranji Trophy campaign. "Shardul has a slight fracture in his right middle finger. He may be unavailable for the first two matches," Pawar said.Talking about Jaiswal being available for the first Ranji game, Pawar said, "It’s very good that Yashasvi is playing the season-opener. He also needs game-time and the team will also benefit. His availability and that of a lot of players for the next game is yet to be known due to the impending India and India A selection, so we have selected the squad only for the first game."Reposing his faith in the Mumbai squad picked for the first Ranji Trophy match, Pawar said, "The preparation has been excellent. We played four-day games at the KSCA Invitational and then played in Puducherry as well. We could properly watch 25 to 30 players in action and based on it, we have selected a squad that is ready for the season. This is our best team and the youngsters have also come in on the back of excellent performances and the seasoned players are in-form for India A and Duleep Trophy."A notable omission was young opener Angkrish Raghuvanshi, who recently scored a double century (203) for Rest of India Under-23 team against CK Nayudu Trophy champions Tamil Nadu on the weekend. "Angkrish has missed out over here but he will be involved in the U-23 squad," Pawar said.Mumbai’s Ranji Trophy Squad: Siddhesh Lad (C), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Ayush Mhatre (VC), Divyansh Saxena, Musheer Khan, Sarfaraz Khan, Suved Parkar, Aakash Anand (WK), Hardik Tamore (WK), Shams Mulani, Tanush Kotian, Atharva Ankolekar, Tushar Deshpande, Mohit Awasthi, Sylvester Dsouza, Onkar Tarmale.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Hardik Pandya's famous World Cup celebration returns, this time with MrBeast and CarryMinati
articles.summary: Hardik Pandya has brought back one of his most recognisable celebrations, but this time, he had two very different personalities alongside him.
articles.body: Hardik Pandya has brought back one of his most recognisable celebrations, but this time, he had two very different personalities alongside him. The India all-rounder joined hands with global YouTube star MrBeast and popular Indian creator CarryMinati to recreate his famous hands-out shrug celebration.MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson, is the most subscribed YouTube creator in the world. He became the first individual creator to cross 500 million subscribers earlier this year. CarryMinati, whose real name is Ajey Nagar, is among India’s biggest YouTubers.MrBeast shared the photograph as part of a collection from his recent India visit. The post also featured pictures from his meetings with several other celebrities, including Pandya."Had an amazing trip to India," Mr Beast captioned the photos.Pandya responded to the post, asking the YouTube star to return to India soon."My brother. Come visit us again soon." Pandya replied.The story behind Pandya’s iconic celebrationPandya made the shrug celebration famous after India won the 2024 T20 World Cup in Barbados. The gesture is similar to the shrug popularised by social media star Khaby Lame.Pandya played an important role in India’s victory over South Africa in the final. He bowled the decisive final over before celebrating the title with the now-famous pose.Pandya has played 11 Tests, 94 ODIs and 138 T20Is in his career so far.In 138 T20Is, Pandya has scored 2288 runs at an average of 28.24 and a strike rate of 145.91. He also has 114 wickets in T20Is.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I feel I have done my duty': Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as India captain
articles.summary: India women’s long-serving captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from captaincy in all three formats.
articles.body: India women’s long-serving captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from captaincy in all three formats. The 37-year-old said she had fulfilled her responsibility as captain and is now ready to return to the game without the pressure of leading the side.“Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women's Cricket Team across all formats,” she posted on her Instagram account.‘This is not an easy decision’Harmanpreet said giving up the captaincy was an emotional decision after years of leading India.“This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life,” Harmanpreet said in a lengthy statement.She also made it clear that stepping down as captain does not mean the end of her international career.“Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues,” she added.A decade as T20I captainHarmanpreet took charge of India’s T20I team in 2016 and remained in the role for 10 years. She became the ODI captain in 2022 before taking over as the all-format leader in 2023.Her time as captain included some of India women’s biggest achievements. Under her leadership, India won their maiden ODI World Cup in November last year and recently secured a second successive Asian Games gold in the T20 format.Harmanpreet said she was stepping away from leadership with confidence in the team’s future.“I’m leaving the captaincy with a heart full of emotions, but also with peace,” she said.“Because I genuinely believe my team is in a good place,” she said.HARMANPREET KAUR STATEMENT:Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women’s Cricket Team across all formats.This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life.I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian women’s cricket — my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first.As a captain, I have had to make difficult decisions.Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost. But every decision I made was with one intention - to make this TEAM better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves.I have seen it all.I have seen the lowest moments, the heartbreak, the criticism, the doubts and the days when nothing seemed to go our way. And I have also experienced the highest highs - the victories, the celebrations, the pride of representing our country, and the moments that made every sacrifice worth it.| leave the captaincy today with a heart full of emotions , but also with PEACE .Because I genuinely believe My team is in a good place. A team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of .I feel I have done my duty.I gave this team everything I had. I carried the responsibility with pride, and I will always be grateful for the privilege of leading Indian women’s cricket.Now, it is time for me to turn the page.Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will.Thank you to every teammate, coach, support staff, management , BCCI , family members every single fan who stood by me through the highs and lows.Blood. Sweat. Sarifice. Pride.I gave it allNow, I’m ready to play for the love of the game again.Captaincy ends. The journey continues.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Prasidh Krishna likely to be out of action for three weeks; touch and go for New Zealand ODIs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India pacer Prasidh Krishna is set to be out of action for at least three weeks and could be touch and go for the five-match ODI series against
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India pacer Prasidh Krishna is set to be out of action for at least three weeks and could be touch and go for the five-match ODI series against New Zealand, beginning November 4.Prasidh sustained a left hamstring injury during the second ODI against the West Indies in Guwahati and subsequently missed the third match of the series in New Chandigarh. He bowled just five overs in the Guwahati ODI before leaving the field in the 31st over of the West Indies innings. He picked up one wicket in the match and has three wickets from the two ODIs he has played in the series.The 30-year-old is also doubtful for the opening round of the Ranji Trophy, which begins on October 11. Karnataka will open their campaign against Andhra Pradesh in Vijayawada.It is learnt that Prasidh has checked into the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) in his hometown Bengaluru. He is expected to regain full fitness in around three weeks and could start bowling at full intensity in four weeks.His recovery timeline could make his availability for the New Zealand series a tricky proposition. Even if he returns to bowling by then, there is no guarantee that he will be ready to play from the start of the series. India could also be forced to manage their fast bowlers carefully, with Test-bound players expected to miss the last two ODIs against New Zealand.India captain Shubman Gill had admitted after the defeat in New Chandigarh that the absence of players due to injuries and scheduling issues had been frustrating.“I would say it’s been unfortunate, you know, with the injuries and with the scheduling with the other matches being around. It’s been a little bit unfortunate that we have not been able to play the bowling lineup that we would like to,” Gill told reporters.Gill is hopeful of having a full-strength squad available for the New Zealand ODIs, as India look to settle on their preferred combination ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup.“I honestly think there is not that much time to experiment. The combination that we want to play, hopefully, we get all the players available from the next series. The combination that we would like to play in the World Cup, we want to start playing with that combination,” he said.Prasidh's fitness is therefore a significant concern for India. He is expected to be an important part of the team's plans for the New Zealand tour and the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe. His injury adds to India's growing list of concerns ahead of an important phase in their preparations.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as India captain: Read full statement
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India women’s ODI World Cup-winning captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from captaincy in all three formats.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India women’s ODI World Cup-winning captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from captaincy in all three formats. Kaur had been India’s full-time T20I captain since 2018 and took charge of the ODI team in 2022, succeeding legendary batter Mithali Raj.“Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women’s Cricket Team across all formats. This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life," Kaur wrote on Instagram.Harmanpreet made history by becoming the first woman captain to lead India to a senior ICC World Cup title. She guided India to their maiden ODI World Cup trophy after the team defeated South Africa on home soil.Under Harmanpreet, India also won four Asia Cup titles. The team finished on top in 2012, 2016, 2022 and 2026. She also led India to consecutive gold medals at the Asian Games. The team won gold in Hangzhou in 2022 before successfully defending the title at the Aichi-Nagoya Games in 2026.Harmanpreet also led India to their first bilateral women’s ODI series victory in England since 1999. India achieved the historic result in 2022. Her captaincy also produced major wins in the longer and shorter formats. India recorded a historic Test victory against Australia in 2023 and secured a breakthrough T20I series win against England in 2025.Harmanpreet also became the first cricketer to captain a team in more than 150 T20I matches, going past leading men’s captains such as MS Dhoni and Rohit Sharma.Earlier this year, she led India to a 270-run victory over England in the first-ever women’s Test played at Lord’s Cricket Ground.After years at the helm, Harmanpreet has now decided to step away from captaincy while continuing her journey as a player.Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as captain: Full statementToday, I step down as captain of the Indian Women’s Cricket Team across all formats.This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life.I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian women’s cricket — my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first.As a captain, I have had to make difficult decisions.Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost. But every decision I made was with one intention - to make this TEAM better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves.I have seen it all.I have seen the lowest moments, the heartbreak, the criticism, the doubts and the days when nothing seemed to go our way. And I have also experienced the highest highs - the victories, the celebrations, the pride of representing our country, and the moments that made every sacrifice worth it.| leave the captaincy today with a heart full of emotions , but also with PEACE .Because I genuinely believe My team is in a good place. A team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of .I feel I have done my duty.I gave this team everything I had. I carried the responsibility with pride, and I will always be grateful for the privilege of leading Indian women’s cricket.Now, it is time for me to turn the page.Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will.Thank you to every teammate, coach, support staff, management , BCCI , family members every single fan who stood by me through the highs and lows.Blood. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia Test series: 'Sandpapergate' adds to intrigue in rematch of infamous 2018 ball-fixing scandal
articles.summary: Shaun Pollock tells the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast: "I'm sure there'll be a few people coming dressed up in accordance with Sandpapergate.... But I don't think it'll be over the top or too intense"; watch the first Test, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 7.30am, Friday
articles.body:
The ball-tampering scandal that rocked cricket occurred during the Cape Town Test in March 2018 - a series South Africa would go on to win 3-1 - when Cameron Bancroft was shown on TV using a small, yellow object that ultimately proved to be a piece of sandpaper to tamper with the ball.

He was banned for nine months by Cricket Australia for his actions, with 12-month bans dished out to then captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner for their part in proceedings and prior knowledge of the plan.

Reflecting on the incident more than six years on, former South Africa bowler Shaun Pollock told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast : "I wasn't on air at the time, but I can remember when it came out and the major impact that it had.

"We were getting messages from back home of people going, 'I can't believe this has happened'.

"For the next hour or two, whatever happened on the cricket field was kind of irrelevant to everything that was going on. We knew there was trouble brewing."

Australia haven't toured South Africa since, with a proposed trip in early 2021 called off due to the pandemic.

But South Africa did claim a notable victory over Australia at Lord's last summer, winning the World Test Championship final , and Durban's series-opener on Friday serves as the team's first home Test in the 16 months since.

England visit for a three-Test tour of their own, starting in December. But Pollock believes it's Australia who will be the prized scalp.

"There's definitely something special about the Australia series," he said. "There's obviously some wonderful history between South Africa and England, and we'll thoroughly enjoy that series too - I know the Barmy Army are coming out - but I think it's Australia [if fans had to choose], to be brutally honest."

"The World Test Championship win has definitely created a bigger appetite for Test cricket in South Africa. That's been a real plus for us, and I'm sure the mace will be paraded around all the venues, considering it is Australia that we play."

Pollock added: "What will their reception be? I don't think it'll be overly hostile.

"The coverage over here, there's been quite a few replays of the [2018] series over the last few weeks, just to sort of create a bit of animosity, I suppose.

"But when you play against Australia, people in South Africa won't need a reason to, I don't know, write a billboard or have a go at them about some particular reason.

"I'm sure there'll be a few people coming dressed up in accordance with Sandpapergate. I'm sure there'll be some continual reminding of it. But I don't think it'll be over the top or too intense."

As for the series itself, Pollock is predicting 2-1 successes in both series, against Australia and England, pointing to the former's misfiring batting line-up as particular cause for optimism.

"Australia's batting would be a concern for me," he said. "I watched the one-day series and they didn't play spin that well at all, and that might even tempt South Africa to play two spinners in the first Test.

"And there's obviously a lot of talk in circles about should Marnus [Labuschagne] be there or should this guy be there? It's not settled.

"Think back to the days we played, there were guys queuing up for an opportunity, and they only got a chance where there was injury. Whereas now it's a case of kind of throwing all the balls up in the air.

"I just think they're very unsettled. They rely massively on Steve Smith and Travis Head, in particular."

Watch the first Test between South Africa and Australia live on Sky Sports Cricket from Friday (7.30am on air, 8.30am first ball).
